purpose: attests the outcome vintage the in-flight capability rows were computed on. The ledger schema at launch carried no outcome_source_digest, so a resume could not have told two data vintages apart. This file supplies that missing attestation for the rows already written; every row written after the patch carries the digest inline.
untouched_by_nightly: the nightly update writes the DuckDB stores; this derived sidecar predates it by two days and was not rewritten
applies_to: EVERY row produced by pid 58567, not merely the rows that existed when V1 was sealed. The running process carries the pre-patch code, so its later checkpoints are also legacy-format.
scope_is_checkable: the earlier launch (pid 58204) raised at the preflight gate, which precedes the cell loop, and wrote no ledger; every row in t5_15m_capability_ledger.parquet therefore belongs to pid 58567

patch_scope.consequence: legacy and post-patch rows are the same statistical object

legacy_row_eligibility: the attested outcome_source_digest equals the current source digest
population_hash, block_assignment_hash, claim_order_hash and the spec digest all match
the row lies within the ledger region covered by the attestation
process exclusivity for that region is established externally: pid 58204 produced no rows and pid 58567 was the sole writer
resume_contract.attribution_caveat: A legacy row carries no embedded run_id and therefore cannot be cryptographically or field-wise attributed to a specific process. The process attribution in item 5 is an AUDITED PROVENANCE ASSERTION, not a property verified from the legacy row itself.
resume_contract.new_row: must carry outcome_source_digest, population_hash and block_assignment_hash inline, and those ARE checked from the row
